correctness.rationale: Every ±1 sign halfspace reduces exactly to ||x||_1≤n(1−ε), so gauge=max(||x||∞,||x||_1/[n(1−ε)]). For half-normal Y_i=|X_i|, M=maxY_i, S=sumY_i, defect E[(S/[n(1−ε)]−M)_+]. Condition on the unique a.s. maximizing coordinate m, use gaps z_j=m−Y_j for other n−1 coordinates and exact support Σz<nεm. For ε<1/n upper bound z_j<m automatically, so no missed boundary. Change variables z_j=εm w_j gives ε^n m^n times fixed simplex domain; dominated convergence for each fixed n is justified by bounded f and integrable m^n f(m). Simplex integral n^n/n!, half-normal moment (2/π)^(n/2)·(1/2)·(2/n)^((n+1)/2) Γ((n+1)/2), giving c_n=2^(n−1/2)n^((n−1)/2)Γ((n+1)/2)/(n!π^(n/2)), positive. The support geometry, normalization including maximizing-index factor n and gauge denominator n, and fixed-dimension limits were independently checked. Packaged `verify.py` checks moment arithmetic only, not an infinite proof.
